Zero-inflated negative binomial regression

zinbreg.Rd

Fits a zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression model. With probability \(\pi_i\) observation \(i\) is a structural zero; with probability \(1-\pi_i\) it comes from an NB(\(\mu_i, \theta\)) distribution, where \(\log\mu_i = x_i^\top\beta + o_i\) and \(\mathrm{logit}\,\pi_i = z_i^\top\gamma\). The model is fitted by an EM algorithm whose M-steps are IRLS fits. No general-purpose optimizer is used.

Usage

zinbreg(
  formula,
  data,
  offset,
  control = zinbreg_control(),
  weights,
  subset,
  na.action
)

Arguments

formula

A two-part formula y ~ x1 + x2 | z1 + z2: count-model covariates before the |, zero-model covariates after it. Without |, the same covariates are used in both parts. Offsets (count part only) may be given with offset() terms before the |.

data

An optional data frame containing the variables in the model.

offset

An optional offset for the count model (e.g. log exposure), added to any offset() terms in the formula.

control

A list of control parameters; see zinbreg_control().

weights

Optional non-negative prior weights \(a_i\).

subset

Optional expression selecting the rows of data to use.

na.action

How to handle missing values (default: the na.action option, usually stats::na.omit()).

Value

An object of class "zinbreg", a list with components

coefficients

List with elements count (\(\beta\)) and zero (\(\gamma\)).

vcov

Covariance matrix of \((\hat\beta, \hat\gamma, \log\hat\theta)\); vcov.zinbreg() returns the block for the coefficients.

theta, SE.theta, log_theta, SE.log_theta

\(\hat\theta\), \(\log\hat\theta\), and their standard errors.

loglik, loglik_path

Maximized observed-data log-likelihood, and its value at the start and after each EM iteration.

df

Number of estimated parameters (\(p + q + 1\)).

iter, converged

Number of EM iterations and convergence flag.

fitted.values

\((1-\hat\pi_i)\hat\mu_i\), the fitted mean.

mu, pi, tau

\(\hat\mu_i\), \(\hat\pi_i\), and the final posterior probabilities \(\tau_i\).

residuals

Response residuals \(y_i - (1-\hat\pi_i)\hat\mu_i\).

y, offset, prior.weights, nobs, df.residual

Response, count offset, prior weights, number of observations with positive weight, and \(n - p - q - 1\).

call, formula, terms, model, xlevels, contrasts, na.action, control

Information about the fit; terms, xlevels and contrasts are lists with count and zero elements.

Algorithm

Starting values: \((\beta, \theta)\) from an NB fit (as in nbreg()); \(\gamma\) from a logistic regression of \(I(y_i = 0)\) on \(z_i\), fitted by IRLS. Then repeat:

  1. E-step. Posterior probability of a structural zero, \(\tau_i = \pi_i / \{\pi_i + (1-\pi_i) f_{NB}(0;\mu_i,\theta)\}\) if \(y_i = 0\), and \(\tau_i = 0\) if \(y_i > 0\).

  2. M-step, zero part. Maximize \(\sum_i a_i\{\tau_i\log\pi_i + (1-\tau_i)\log(1-\pi_i)\}\): a logistic regression with fractional response \(\tau_i\), fitted by IRLS with \(w_i = a_i\pi_i(1-\pi_i)\) and working response \(z_i^\top\gamma + (\tau_i-\pi_i)/\{\pi_i(1-\pi_i)\}\).

  3. M-step, count part. Maximize \(\sum_i a_i(1-\tau_i)\log f_{NB}(y_i;\mu_i,\theta)\): the NB fit of nbreg() with prior weights \(a_i(1-\tau_i)\).

until the observed-data log-likelihood changes by less than control$tol. EM never decreases the log-likelihood; the path is stored in loglik_path, and a warning is given if it ever decreases.

Standard errors come from the inverse of the observed information, \(-\partial^2\ell/\partial\psi\partial\psi^\top\), with \(\psi = (\beta, \gamma, \log\theta)\), computed from the analytic second derivatives of the observed-data log-likelihood at the MLE. \(\mathrm{SE}(\hat\theta) = \hat\theta\,\mathrm{SE}(\log\hat\theta)\) (delta method).

References

Lambert, D. (1992). Zero-inflated Poisson regression, with an application to defects in manufacturing. Technometrics, 34(1), 1-14.

Zeileis, A., Kleiber, C. and Jackman, S. (2008). Regression models for count data in R. Journal of Statistical Software, 27(8), 1-25.

See also

zinbreg_control(), nbreg()

Examples

set.seed(2)
n <- 500
x <- rnorm(n)
z <- rnorm(n)
structural_zero <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-1 + 1 * z))
y <- ifelse(structural_zero == 1, 0,
            rnbinom(n, mu = exp(1 + 0.5 * x), size = 2))
fit <- zinbreg(y ~ x | z)
fit
#> 
#> Call:
#> zinbreg(formula = y ~ x | z)
#> 
#> Count model coefficients (negbin with log link):
#> (Intercept)            x  
#>      0.9658       0.4699  
#> Theta = 2.291 
#> 
#> Zero-inflation model coefficients (binomial with logit link):
#> (Intercept)            z  
#>     -0.9633       1.0990  
#> 
#> Log-likelihood: -871.451 on 5 df
#> 
summary(fit)
